messages:
dylan: heads up — canary for dedicated pool 'eu-west-reserved' (canary id c-42) is showing sustained p99 increases after the autobatch/kernel-selection merge that landed in main ~2h ago
maya: on it. what's the magnitude? any customer impact yet?
dylan: p50 stable, p95 up ~10%, p99 up ~60-80% depending on seq len. saw timeouts on 2 canary pods; infra restarted one. stack traces point at kv-prefetcher loops + unexpected kernel selection changes
maya: hmm. any logs/trace snippets we can paste?
dylan: pasted below from canary pod (abridged):
```
2026-03-18T14:12:23Z runtime: selecting kernel matmul_opt_v2 for model:gptx-large seq=1024
2026-03-18T14:12:23Z kv-prefetch: scheduled prefetch for key-range=0..512, hit=0.2
2026-03-18T14:12:23Z runtime: selected kernel matmul_fallback with different tiling
2026-03-18T14:12:24Z kv-prefetch: evict-loop start, queued=34, inflight=2
2026-03-18T14:12:25Z perf: token-gen step 0.45s (expected 0.08s), p99 spike
```
maya: looks like the kernel selector flipped between candidates mid-request, and kv-prefetcher started thrashing evictions — could be contention on the KV manager locks
raj: this smells like the recent change that lets the selector prefer memory-friendly kernels when cache pressure is high. If prefetch metrics are wrong we'll get oscillation
lee: I reproduced on my local dedicated stack with the canary image. Running a synthetic load with seq=1024 and a 10% long-tail of 4096 triggers the thrash in ~2 minutes. Profiling shows high time in `kv_manager::evict_if_needed` and `kernel_router::choose_candidate`
dylan: CI perf check didn't catch it because our unit workload used seq<=512 only. we need a short perf test for longseq-heavy traffic in canary gating
maya: agree — temporary mitigation: disable the new memory-pref kernel preference flag on canary and pause rollout?
deploy-bot: Deploy attempted: canary/c-42 -> rollout paused by automation: high-latency-detector triggered (p99 threshold breached) :warning:
raj: +1 on pause. Also suggest reverting the selector commit if we confirm it's the root cause. I have a bisect plan: revert selector change locally, run longseq load to confirm.
dylan: bisect in progress — testing revert of commit 0f3b9c2 (selector mem-pref). will report in 15m
ana: (typo: ana) small prod note — we have one enterprise customer on that pool with soft SLOs. I've notified customer-success to hold off on heavy jobs and offered to move traffic temporarily to another dedicated pool
lee: bisect result: reverting 0f3b9c2 removes the thrash. p99 returns to baseline. Looks like the selector was overreacting to transient cache pressure and triggering a kernel swap that invalidates cached KV layouts
maya: ok that's pretty conclusive. options: revert commit in main, push hotfix toggle to disable mem-pref behavior, or tune the eviction thresholds + make selector less sensitive
raj: i'd prefer the toggle + threshold tune as fast mitigation (smaller blast radius). put revert on standby if toggle doesn't stabilize canary in 30m
dylan: created PR to add runtime flag `--selector-stability-window=200ms` and default to old behavior for now. linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
maya: good. roll back canary image to previous stable until PR lands? or flip flag via config in canary env?
lee: flipping the flag in canary config is faster. applying now.
dylan: applied config change to canary, monitoring... p99 down to ~baseline after ~90s.
deploy-bot: Canary c-42 config update applied by dylan — health check passing
maya: excellent. keep this thread for postmortem. action items: 1) PR for stability window (#4821) 2) add longseq perf test to CI gating 3) add KV-prefetch metrics to canary dashboards 4) consider kernel selection unit tests for oscillation scenarios
raj: i'll own 2 and 3. assigning to myself in jira
dylan: i'll follow up on 1, and open an incident report draft for customer-notify record
ana: thanks all — glad we caught this in canary. :thumbsup:
maya: closing the canary hold once PR merged and we run 1 full canary cycle. will update calendar slot for a re-roll tomorrow morning
lee: note for postmortem: include flame graphs for `evict_if_needed` and `choose_candidate`, and a short sequence diagram of selector <> kv-manager interactions
---
Context/notes: reproduced regression is tied to merge that changed kernel selection heuristics to prioritize memory-friendly kernels under cache pressure. regression manifested as KV-prefetch eviction thrash + kernel swap mid-request causing work duplication and p99 spikes. paused rollout, applied config toggle to stabilize canary, bisected to selector commit, follow-up PR created to add stability window and CI longseq test. No confirmed customer impact beyond one soft-SLO customer; CS notified.
